concept.anti_generic_signature: A thick pillow-rounded lunar cabochon with a star suspended inside the negative-space cradle on one visibly intentional beam, not a flat crescent plaque or loose charm.
assumptions: A rigid one-piece FDM print is the desired artifact rather than a separately moving star.
A smooth hard tabletop permits the continuous outer arc to rock through the illustrated poses.

components.form: Thick extruded crescent with rounded finite-width horn ends.
components.interfaces: Fused continuously to the radial bridge; outer arc contacts the play surface.
components.name: Rocking crescent body
components.placement: Forms the full outer body around the central negative space.
components.purpose: Provides the recognizable moon silhouette and continuous gravity-rocking contact arc.

components.form: Smooth five-lobed star extruded to the full body depth.
components.interfaces: Fused to the inner end of the radial bridge.
components.name: Captive star
components.placement: Suspended within the crescent opening near the inner center.
components.purpose: Supplies the climbing celestial subject at the center of the rocking gesture.

components.form: Broad rectangular radial beam with fused overlaps at both ends.
components.interfaces: Boolean-fused into both crescent and star as one printable solid.
components.name: Radial star bridge
components.placement: Runs from the crescent inner wall to the star.
components.purpose: Makes the moon-star relationship mechanically truthful while preserving the open silhouette.

concept.construction: One fused print: circular-arc crescent body, five-point star, and broad radial bridge; flat-back print orientation, no supports or assembly.
concept.hardest_to_fake_magic: Across exactly three physical rocking poses, the joined star must seem to climb the crescent's inner sky and return, even though moon and star are one body.
concept.intended_interaction: Set the flat extruded toy on its continuous outer arc, nudge either reinforced horn to rock it upward, and release so gravity returns it to its starting pose.
concept.signature_decision: Fuse the star inside the crescent on one visible radial bridge so the celestial pair reads immediately and the star appears to climb as the whole rigid silhouette rocks.
concept.signature_interaction: Nudge a horn: the continuous circular back carries the joined star from the -26 degree start to the +26 degree crest, then release returns the same rigid body to the -26 degree start pose.
concept.summary: A one-piece crescent-and-star desk toy that turns a small nudge into a legible rise-and-return rocking gesture.
concept.title: Orbit Cradle
unresolved_risks: Digital checks cannot establish real-world damping, rocking duration, print finish, or human response without a physical prototype.

research.evidence_plan: Check exact BREP solidity and dimensions, exported STL watertightness/bed contact/thickness, render the exact mesh in three Z-axis poses, and bind an independent blind visual read to the final image hashes.
research.limits: Digital geometry checks do not prove a successful physical print, real damping, surface finish, or measured rocking duration.
research.method: Pico Press gravity-and-balance construction, using a broad continuous contact arc and a complete one-handed rock/reset cycle.
research.print_strategy: The monolithic object prints on a 24 mm deep flat back; rounded front and perimeter transitions rise gradually, with no trapped cavities or separate parts.
